(“QXO” or the “Company”) is a leading distributor and installer of building products in North America. QXO plans to become the tech-enabled leader in the $800 billion building products distribution and installation industry and is targeting $ 50 billion in annual revenues within the next decade through accretive acquisitions and organic growth. Prior to the Beacon Acquisition (as defined below), QXO was primarily a technology solutions and professional services company, providing critical software applications, consulting and other professional services. The acquisitions of Beacon, Kodiak and TopBuild have expanded the Company’s scale, product and service offerings, geographic reach and customer base. In North America, QXO is the largest distributor and installer of insulation, the second-largest distributor of roofing products, the second-largest publicly traded distributor of lumber and building materials, and the largest distributor of waterproofing products. The Company serves customers in all 50 states throughout the United States (the “U.S.”) and seven provinces in Canada, including residential, commercial, and industrial general contractors, subcontractors of all types including roofing, insulation, and framing, as well as local, regional, and production homebuilders. Net Sales Net sales represent the consideration the Company expects to be entitled to in exchange for transferring products to customers and, to a lesser extent, providing installation and construction services to customers. The Company recognizes net sales as it satisfies its performance obligations under contracts with customers. Net product sales are generally recognized at a point in time when control of the product transfers to the customer, which occurs when the customer accepts the delivery of the product or takes possession of the product with rights and rewards of ownership. Net service sales, which are comprised of the Company’s installation service contracts, are recognized over time as the related performance obligation is satisfied. Progress toward complete satisfaction of the performance obligation is measured using a cost-to-cost measure of progress method. The cost input is based on the amount of material installed at that customer’s location and the associated labor costs, as compared to the total expected cost for the particular order. The total expected cost is an estimate in the revenue recognition process, which requires judgment, and is subject to variability throughout the duration of the contract as a result of contract modifications and other circumstances impacting job completion. Generally, this results in revenue being recognized as the customer is able to receive and utilize the benefits provided by the Company’s services. Each contract contains one or more individual orders, which are based on services delivered. When product and installation services are bundled in a contract, the Company combines them into one performance obligation as the overall promise is to transfer the combined item. Our Strategy We plan to become the tech-enabled leader in the $800 billion building products distribution and installation industry and are targeting $50 billion in annual revenues within the next decade through accretive acquisitions, including tuck-in acquisitions with the potential for significant bottom-line contributions, and organic growth initiatives. Our growth initiatives are focused on pricing and procurement, cross-selling, private label expansion, branch operations and technology and digital capabilities. We believe stronger pricing, increased cross-selling, greater customer engagement and improved service execution are driving accelerating sales trends and profitable market share gains. Our organic daily revenue trends have improved for the second consecutive quarter. Our goal is to grow Adjusted EBITDA (as defined below) to $4 billion by 2030, before additional acquisitions, reflecting market growth, share gains, productivity improvements and synergies as we integrate Kodiak and TopBuild. In addition, we believe there will continue to be opportunities to purchase small businesses on accretive terms. Between now and 2030, acquisitions that we can fund with our internally generated cash flow could contribute up to approximately $1.5 billion of additional Adjusted EBITDA, taking the total Adjusted EBITDA opportunity to approximately $5.5 billion by 2030. Our operations are highly cash-generative, with no significant debt maturities prior to 2031, a capital structure with limited financial maintenance covenants and over $2 billion of available liquidity, and more than half of our debt is fixed rate. We have substantial flexibility to invest in organic growth and pursue attractive acquisitions. Pricing and Procurement . Our pricing to customers is a major lever for us. We are strengthening pricing discipline through enhanced tools, management oversight and incentives, including tighter controls over excessive price overrides. Our goal is to price intelligently and consistently, in a way that is fair to our customers and to QXO. We believe improved pricing realization is supported by broader product offerings, greater product availability, faster and better customer service and more reliable deliveries, while more consistent pricing practices help us achieve appropriate returns. We generated significant improvements in year-over-year pricing in the third quarter despite the current soft environment. Further opportunities include improving commercial-deal pricing, updating customer-specific prices and linking quoting decisions more closely to customer profitability. We are also extending sophisticated pricing analytics into the acquired businesses. Procurement is another major lever for us. Across Beacon, Kodiak and TopBuild, our current purchasing represents approximately $12 billion of spend, including approximately $11 billion in direct products and materials and more than $1.1 billion in indirect goods and services. We have largely centralized procurement and established centralized category leadership, and are bringing that purchasing scale together across the businesses. We have approximately $7.6 billion of spend with suppliers serving at least two of our three acquired businesses, including over 1,000 direct suppliers and approximately 200 indirect suppliers. Within that overlap, approximately $5.1 billion is with suppliers serving all three acquired businesses. These existing relationships create opportunities to align pricing, rebates and contract terms and negotiate using our combined purchasing volume. We are pursuing purchasing efficiencies by consolidating our supplier base around strategic partners that provide value to our customers and support our growth, 44 Table of Contents as well as through coordinated negotiations, stronger rebate capture and wider adoption of common purchasing agreements. Our goal is to reward strategic supplier partners with more of our purchases, allowing them to rapidly grow with us and helping us improve cost, product availability and service, increasing the value we can add to customers. We have already realized procurement synergies across a number of indirect categories, including fleet, technology and waste disposal. Internal sourcing is also creating value by enabling our businesses to purchase products from one another, reducing reliance on third-party suppliers and retaining more margin within the Company. Cross-selling . Cross-selling is a key focus as we continue to integrate the three companies we acquired. We have approximately 194,000 unique customers, and almost none of them buy our full product offering. We already have relationships with these customers and, in many cases, we are already on their job sites. We have an opportunity to earn a much larger share of their business and create substantial organic growth. Our objective is to reduce customers’ total construction costs while increasing our share of their spending. A production homebuilder, custom builder or general contractor purchasing multiple categories of building materials has a compelling reason to consolidate suppliers and reduce complexity. By combining traditional building supplies with engineered components, including trusses and wall panels, installation services and field management capabilities, we are able to help customers address labor shortages, simplify procurement, improve project coordination and reduce delays. In addition, our relationships with production homebuilders, supported by our truss and wall panel capabilities, provide opportunities to expand sales across our product and service offerings. This integrated offering helps customers complete projects faster and at lower cost while driving growth. Coordinating crews and services can eliminate duplicate trips, reduce material handling, improve scheduling and shorten construction cycles, such as by combining garage door and interior trim installation visits or using an employee already on site to complete work that would otherwise require more personnel. We are also pursuing opportunities to expand cross-selling to commercial and industrial customers and to reactivate acquired dormant customer accounts through superior service reliability and product availability. Our insulation business posted accelerating top-line trends in the third quarter of 2026. Across the businesses we acquired, there is a significant base of dormant customers with substantial aggregate purchasing power, including a number of large customers who together used to do nearly half a billion dollars of business with us. Our improvements in product availability, on-time and in-full delivery, and invoice accuracy give us a stronger value proposition with these customers. Private Label Expansion . We are expanding our private label offerings, which provide a high-quality and superior-value alternative for our customers while delivering higher margins and brand exclusivity in the marketplace. Private label’s gross margin is substantially higher than the margin on similar branded products. Trailing 12-month TRI-BUILT sales were $943 million, all at legacy Beacon, and our target is to grow TRI-BUILT to more than $2 billion in sales over the next three years. Our initiatives to expand TRI-BUILT sales include developing additional product categories, increasing penetration in low-slope roofing, strengthening sales incentives and introducing private label products across the legacy Kodiak and TopBuild businesses. Branch Operations . We are deploying experienced operators to low-performing branches, focusing on increased customer contact, disciplined pricing, appropriate staffing and agile inventory management. These address the fundamentals that determine whether a branch serves customers well and earns an appropriate return. Legacy TopBuild has used this special operations approach effectively in its lower-performing locations, and we are transplanting that process to other parts of QXO. One of the benefits of owning these businesses together is the ability to take a proven operating practice and apply it more broadly. The TopBuild Acquisition gave us additional commercial exposure, including data centers, and a presence at approximately 22,000 job sites daily. This creates substantial opportunities to deepen customer relationships, cross-sell products and services and capture a greater share of construction spending. We are applying best-in-class operating practices across the combined Company and establishing common operating metrics to identify opportunities for greater efficiency across our branch network. Gross margin on our roofing and waterproofing products increased year over year in the third quarter of 2026. Within our installation operations, we are supplementing our highly experienced installers’ technical expertise, including their ability to complete a job efficiently and pass inspection, with enhanced sales management, training for new hires and technology to increase productivity and enable employees to devote more time to their core responsibilities. Technology and Digital Capabilities . We have made meaningful investments in our technology and digital capabilities to transform all aspects of our business, from providing a world-class customer experience to revolutionizing the way we do business. We believe technology will help us accelerate many of these improvements in the coming months. We are connecting a new enterprise resource planning system, a proprietary point-of-sale system, an upgraded customer relationship management platform with advanced artificial intelligence (“AI”) capabilities, and a warehouse management system. We are also integrating capabilities for pricing, procurement, fleet management, e-commerce, human resources, and internal communications. Our goal is for employees to get their work done in one connected, AI-enabled environment, reducing time spent entering information into different systems or tracking down information that should be readily available, and giving our people more time to serve customers and manage the business. We are testing the system in a number of locations in real operating conditions, training employees and identifying improvements in preparation to rapidly expand the rollout. We expect these new platforms to support the vast majority of revenue across the three acquired businesses by the end of 2027.
